messages.subject: mediation analysis with categorical variables
parts:
Hi, I am running a mediation analysis with categorical variables in lavaan. the first model i analysed was not having a good fit. Pat advised I allow the disturbance terms to covary with each other. I  try to do that, but got some warnings and it could not run  the standard errors. Can my model be checked please, probably i did something wrong. I appreciate your usual cooperation. the result is displayed below:

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: mediation analysis with categorical variables
parts:
On 7/28/20 2:14 PM, Paul Joseph wrote:
> fit3<-lavaan(model2,data=mala,ordered=c("medul","hospdel","wsystem1","exbrest","immu","muac"))
> Error in tmp[cbind(row..idx, col..idx)] <- 1 : subscript out of bounds

Here are a few tips:
- use the sem() function instead
- don't specify any (residual) variances/covariances in your model
syntax: the sem() function will add the ones that are needed
- exogenous variables should be declared as ordinal

Yves.

parts:
On 7/31/20 11:47 AM, vikram sridhar wrote:
> Dear yves,
> Can you explain about which method is empliyed to get the standard error
> for all the estimates including indirect effects.

For 'regular' parameters, lavaan uses standard techniques. If
categorical data is involved, the default estimator (WLSMV) uses
'robust' standard errors (see, eg Satorra & Bentler, 1994).

For indirect effects, by default, lavaan uses the 'delta method' to
derive approximate standard errors.

I also noticed that I wrote:

> - exogenous variables should be declared as ordinal

that should be:

- exogenous variables should NOT be declared as ordinal.

Yves.

messages.subject: Re: mediation analysis with categorical variables
parts:
On 8/1/20 4:04 PM, vikram sridhar wrote:
> Dear yves,

> Thanks for your information sir. If we declare the exogenous variable as
> ordinal, what will be the issue? Why we should not declare them as ordinal?

By default, lavaan uses conditional.x = TRUE in the categorical setting.
That means that we do not model the exogenous covariates. We just
condition on them. So we don't need to 'know' if they ordinal/binary or
just continuous. Declaring them as ordinal is redundant.

Yves.
